Theme

Latin word

nēmō

nēmō, nēminis m. and f.

pronoun; in classical Latin gen. nūllīus, abl. nūllō

nobody, no one; none (of persons): none of us, none of them

In this lexicon

  • nobody

    the recommended word · classical · Varr. RR 2.1.2: nēmō enim omnia potest scīre; Cic. Fam. 7.30.1: scītō nēminem prandisse; Traupman 351

  • none

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 58.22: nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē; Verg. A. 5.305: nēmō ex hōc numerō

  • nēmō nōn: everyone

    classical

  • Ultrā posse nēmō obligātur.: no one is obliged to do more than he can

    modern

Examples

  • nēmō enim omnia potest scīre

    for nobody can know everythingVarr. RR 2.1.2

    In the entry for nobody

  • ita Canīniō cōnsule scītō nēminem prandisse

    so, in Caninius’s consulship, let me tell you, nobody had lunchCic. Fam. 7.30.1

    In the entry for nobody

  • itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus

    and so far nobody who wanted to see me has found me busyCic. Sen. 32

    In the entry for nobody

  • Nēmō timendō ad summum pervenit locum.

    Nobody ever reached the top by being afraid.Publil. Sent. N 68

    In the entry for nobody
